description: Build a data quality report of NULL rates per load date for the columns configured in dq_null_thresholds. For each load_date and each configured column of patient_visits (patient_id, diagnosis_code), compute null_pct = 100 * (rows where the column is NULL or, for STRING columns, an empty/whitespace-only string) / total rows of that load_date. Compare with max_null_pct and set is_breach = null_pct > max_null_pct. Output columns: load_date (DATE), column_name (STRING), row_count (INT64), null_pct (FLOAT64, 1 decimal), max_null_pct (FLOAT64), is_breach (BOOL).

patient_id.description: Patient identifier; should never be NULL

diagnosis_code.description: ICD-style code; upstream sometimes sends '' instead of NULL

edge_cases: Empty string and whitespace-only diagnosis_code count as NULL
A load_date with zero NULLs must still produce a row with null_pct = 0.0
Threshold comparison is strict (null_pct equal to the threshold is not a breach)
common_failure_modes: FM5: COUNT(diagnosis_code) treats empty strings as populated, under-reporting the NULL rate
FM3: Integer division or dividing by COUNT(column) instead of COUNT(*) distorts the percentage
FM7: Report omits load dates/columns with no NULLs, so missing rows are indistinguishable from missing checks
